sections.html:
Greenville is the Washington County seat and the largest city in the Mississippi Delta, with 29,670 residents at the 2020 count. It sits on Lake Ferguson, an oxbow lake left by an old channel of the Mississippi River. The city covers about 27.7 square miles, of which roughly 26.9 are land.

It grew as a cotton trading center, and the housing shows it. Several late 1800s and early 1900s buildings are on the National Register of Historic Places, including the Gamwyn Park Historic District. Older houses can carry aging systems, and homes inside a historic district may need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the city before exterior changes. People moving for a job, school or family often need a fixed closing date, and that is where an as-is sale can help.

sections.h2: Heat, cold and the condition of an older house
sections.html:
Summers are long and hot, and winters are mild and damp, so cooling and drainage are standard repair items. Record temperatures run from 106 F in August to 8 F in January.

  • A buyer will test the air conditioning, so know its age and service history.
  • With a record low of 8 F, exposed pipes and older plumbing are worth a look before a buyer's inspector does it.

The City of Greenville's Planning Department covers zoning, building permits, housing inspection and code enforcement. Its staff includes a Planning and Zoning Director, a Building Inspector, a Housing Inspector and a Code Enforcement Officer. The department phone is 662-378-1548.

Permit forms include building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and gas, a fence permit, a sign permit and a Garage, Rummage and Estate Sale Permit. Heirs clearing a house should note that last one, since an estate sale on the property needs a permit.

  • Zoning rules are in Appendix B of the city ordinance.
  • The city has a 20-year strategic plan, linked from its planning page.
  • A Brownfields Assessment grant funds an inventory of underused or possibly contaminated sites, so ask whether your property or a neighbor is part of it.

Start at the city's planning page.

The elected Tax Collector bills and collects property tax for Washington County. Real property taxes are payable by February 1 following the tax year, and the collector's page says 1 percent per month interest is due on any unpaid balance after that date. Once a year the collector must hold a tax sale for unpaid real estate taxes and special assessments.

A short note on timing. The bill follows the previous tax year, the homestead window closes April 1, and the tax sale can fall in April or August. If you plan to list in spring, file homestead first. If you plan to list in summer, check that nothing is open before the August sale date.

The assessor lists and values all real estate in the county, helps owners file for homestead exemption and keeps ownership maps. A tax GIS map linked from the assessor's page shows how your parcel is drawn. Appeals go before the Board of Supervisors, and the usual cutoff is the first Monday in August.

Homestead has strings attached. A person is not eligible if the owner or spouse failed to follow Mississippi income tax laws, and vehicles must be tagged where they are domiciled, which for a homestead is the home. Confirm your status before you list.

A sale here follows the state's standard sequence: disclosure, contract, title work, deed and recording. Mississippi Code Section 89-1-503 wants the buyer to receive a written statement about the property's condition early, as soon as practicable before title moves. A line on the contract or an addendum shows you did it.

The Washington County Chancery Clerk records the deed. Washington County is an archive-fee county, which puts the recording price of a deed at $26.00 with the first five pages indexed, and $1.00 more for every extra page. Mississippi formatting rules for recordable instruments, in place since 2009 and 2021, include a name, address and phone number for the preparer.

Work through it in this order. First, pull the deed and learn exactly who is on title. Second, ask the Tax Collector what is owed. Third, ask the Planning Department about code notices and permits. Fourth, sign a purchase contract. Fifth, let the title company search the record and prepare the closing papers.

  • Confirm all taxes are current so nothing goes to the August tax sale.
  • Ask the Planning Department about open code notices.
  • Locate the recorded deed and any prior mortgage release.
  • Use an attorney or title company, because preparing a deed for a fee is the practice of law in Mississippi.

At the closing table the title company pays the taxes and any mortgage balance out of your proceeds, then sends the new deed to the clerk.

sections.h2: When an as-is cash offer suits a Greenville house
sections.html:
Greenville sellers tend to fall into a few groups, and each has a different first step:

  • Heirs with a vacant house: confirm who has authority to sign, apply for the estate sale permit if you plan to clear contents on site, and clear any code notice.
  • Landlords: gather lease terms so a buyer can see what comes with the house.
  • Owners behind on taxes: ask the Tax Collector for a payoff amount, then choose between paying it now and letting the sale cover it.
  • Owners relocating: choose a closing date first, then match the buyer and the paperwork to it.

It suits a house where repairs, an estate or a code notice would push a conventional sale past your timeline. Cash Home Buyers looks at houses in the condition they are in, including older homes with deferred maintenance, so you do not have to finish fixes first.

Whichever way you lean, compare the paths side by side. A repaired and listed house may sell for more on paper, but agent fees, repair bills and months of carrying costs come out of that number. A written cash offer lets you see the other side clearly and decline it if it does not work.

Even then, compare options. Ask what repairs would cost, what a listing would require and how long each path would take. The legal steps stay the same either way.

faqs.q: When are Washington County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real property taxes are payable by February 1 after the tax year. The county collector says 1 percent per month interest applies after that, and unpaid real estate taxes go to an annual tax sale.

faqs.q: Does Greenville require a permit for an estate sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The Planning Department lists a Garage, Rummage and Estate Sale Permit among its forms, so heirs should apply before holding a sale. Call 662-378-1548 to confirm current requirements.

faqs.q: Where do I file for homestead exemption in Greenville?
faqs.a: Go to the Washington County Tax Assessor, whose office helps homeowners file. The window is January 1 to April 1, and a filing stays in effect until your status changes.

faqs.q: Who can appeal a Washington County assessment?
faqs.a: An owner who believes the value is too high can request a hearing before the county Board of Supervisors. Do it by the first Monday in August.

faqs.q: Do historic district homes in Greenville need extra approval?
faqs.a: Exterior changes to properties in the Historic District may need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the city. The Planning Department can tell you whether your address is covered.
